messages.subject: Rcpp 0.9.14 & clang++ 3.1?
parts:
I noticed Dirk released a new Rcpp, 0.9.1.4.
I do wonder if we'll ever get a version 1 :-)

Specifically, though I was wondering about this:

On 10/1/12 3:37 PM, Dirk Eddelbuettel wrote:
...
> * Be more conservative about where we support
> clang++ and the inclusion of
> exception_defines.h and prevent this from
> being attempted on OS X where it failed for
> clang 3.1

I couldn't tell if this mean it would or wouldn't
work with clang++ 3.1, which is the version of clang++
distributed with Xcode on Mac OS X.

Also, I'm not sure if this matters, because I'm not
sure how much RStan lets us customize compilers.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Rcpp 0.9.14 & clang++ 3.1?
parts:
I made a diff between Rcpp 0.9.14 and 0.9.13, which tells me 
essentially nothing related really changed.  Then I did not 
understand what Dirk said regarding clang.  But who cares.
So the bottom line is that the new version would not have any 
new impact on RStan. 

RStan allow those users who know how to change the c++ compiler to 
change that just as those compiler flags.  In essential, RStan do not 
control what compiler is used, it just use package inline, which calls
`R CMD SHLIB`.  R CMD SHLIB will call GNU make, which will
use whatever is configure in those Makevars files at different places. 

I guess there is/was some problem with Rcpp (current version
and previous version) if clang++ (version before 3.1?).

--
Jiqiang
